text.p: The French government gave the following details of a revised 1996 budget, approved by the cabinet on Wednesday, in an official statement released on Thursday. Budget Minister Alain Lamassoure announced most of the key factors in the revised budget on Wednesday.
CENTRAL GOVERNMENT BUDGET DEFICIT
Fixed at 287.985 billion francs, compared to 287.807 in the initial Finance Act.
The total public deficit -- which includes welfare and local authority spending -- will be capped at four percent of gross domestic product.
SPENDING

The revised budget takes account of 23 billion francs in new spending. The two biggest areas of new spending are 4.9 billion in additional capital injections to state-owned firms and 4.7 billion in housing aid.
Most of the spending increases have been offset by savings elsewhere, leaving a net rise in spending of 3.3 billion francs.
SAVINGS
The main savings came from:
-- 6.4 billion francs in lower debt service charges thanks to the fall in interest rates.
-- 1.5 billion francs from all government ministries through scrapping planned spending lines.

-- 6.8 billion francs from the Special Treasury Accounts, due to an underestimation of the amount expected to be raised from local authority taxes. The state lends money to local authorities for their running costs, based on an estimate of the amount expected from local taxes.
REVENUES
Total receipts were 3.2 billion francs more than expected.
Tax receipts were 22.8 billion francs less than expected, mainly due to a 22.1 billion franc shortfall in Value Added Tax (sales tax), hit by weak economic growth.
The shortfall in tax receipts was offset by 17.2 billion francs in extra non-tax receipts.
Ministers said these came from:
-- Withdrawal of old banknotes from circulation
-- Contribution from state bank Caisse des Depots et Consignation
-- Contribution from export credit guarantee agency Coface
-- Savings from lower cost of funding Credit Foncier cheap housing loans due to the fall in interest rates
Charges on revenues will be 8.8 billion francs less than expected, largely due to a 7.8 billion franc reduction in France's contribution to the European Union budget.
